tiles.heading: Look here first
tiles.details: CANYON MUHLY ×involuta is an accepted CENTRAL-TEXAS natural hybrid M. lindheimeri × M. reverchonii. NOW actual source-labelled live botanical photographs are LOCATED at UT Austin PlantPics (Bob Harms): habit (MUIN-a), open head with ruler (MUIN-I), and collar/ligule with ruler (MUIN-L). This eliminates the assumption that no real photograph exists, but the UT use terms and whole-site photo count still must be checked before rehosting. The canonical gallery remains a historical multi-taxon plate plus parent photos until import is legal. For reliable ID: fresh FIRM DECURRENT brown-based ligule, tightly folded blades, 3–4 mm spikelets, ~2–2.5 mm glumes and 0.5–2 mm awn. Verify specimen/hybrid origin; intermediate bunch size alone is NOT proof.

tiles.heading: Look-alike comparison
tiles.details: Lindheimer generally makes a larger, coarser more erect bunch with comparatively contracted dense flowering branches; seep muhly makes a smaller fine tuft with an airy delicate head. This natural hybrid may be intermediate and is particularly risky to force from habit-only photos. Ornamental pink-flowered M. capillaris is not a substitute ID.

panels.label: 1 · CANYON MUHLY — real living hybrid clumps in habitat
panels.image_role: Real source-identified whole Muhlenbergia involuta plant habitat photo, copyrighted Bob Harms
panels.caption: Bob Harms's true canyon muhly photograph shows several substantial pale-green clumps on a dry rocky Central Texas-looking slope. Multiple clumps may overlap in the photo: an individual root crown cannot be traced, and its ligule, spikelets and exact fertile hybrid status are not independently resolved here.
panels.why_it_matters: This is the first actual source-labelled LIVE canyon muhly habit photograph for the learner, not an intermediate-looking parent substituted for the hybrid.

panels.label: 2 · CANYON MUHLY — flowering panicle and scale
panels.image_role: Real source-labelled canyon muhly detached or isolated flowering panicle, ruler visible on right
panels.caption: The narrow upright loose panicle has widely separated slender branches and individual elongated/ovoid pale spikelets; a ruler appears along the right edge. This is NOT a same-root field habit photograph and does not show the true blade collar or exact lemma awn origin.
panels.why_it_matters: Identify the broad panicle architecture and separate a whole branch from a small spikelet; use the scale only where the part can actually be measured.

panels.label: 3 · CANYON MUHLY — distinct panicle branch/spikelets
panels.image_role: Real source-labelled canyon muhly flowering closeup with actual spikelets along thin branches
panels.caption: Separate slender, sometimes branching stalks each carry small pale narrow spikelets. Some awnlike projections are visible, but this frame does NOT independently establish the glume, lemma lengths, 3-nerved lemma or an exact 0.5–2 mm awn insertion.

panels.label: 4 · CANYON MUHLY — true leaf sheath/collar with scale
panels.image_role: Real source-labelled canyon muhly leaf sheath junction/ligule region photographed beside graduated scale
panels.caption: Bob Harms photographed the actual upper sheath/blade junction, including thin pale sheath margins and a narrow membranous tissue near the collar. The image includes a ruler. It does not clearly isolate a single free ligule attachment throughout its base, so do NOT place an anatomical arrow declaring this detail confirmed by image alone; verify the intact ligule under hand lens.
panels.why_it_matters: Provides the first exact-species collar photo, an important tie-breaker from seep and Lindheimer's muhly. Measure only clearly bounded structures.
